# Does the first evaluator's decision path predict the next evaluator's vote?

The public AE test release was previously inspected. Its 9,724 judgments include four distinct decision paths, two common paths and two less common paths for negative votes. Fit lookup tables on its repeatedly rated items. Evaluate once on the publisher's dev release after excluding every question ID present in the fitting release (including singly rated items). Call this reverse-split transfer within a single dataset. Retain all eligible items and ordered distinct judgment pairs. Average within item and then equally across items. Aggregate by question for paired uncertainty.

Primary method estimates the probability of a second positive judgment conditional on the first reader's raw decision path. Smooth each path's training sum toward the empirical conditional mean given its binary vote with two pseudo-observations. Each training item contributes total mass one spread across its ordered pairs. Compare with the collapsed empirical binary transition table, training marginal, first binary vote, and unsmoothed path table. Unseen paths back off to the binary transition table. Report Brier and natural log loss with all probabilities clipped to [.01,.99]. Use cluster-robust conditional 95% intervals for each Brier comparison and report how many questions survive disjointness screening. If no multiply rated questions survive, record the feasibility failure. This tests incremental value of an existing reader's released intermediate responses and cannot establish rater-specific behavior or generalize to essay scoring. No model selection on the evaluation labels.
